Extracellular contrast agents (Gd) #23

  • 1) Gd: Hyperosmolarity, strongly paramagnetic (7 unpaired
  • electrons)
  • 2) Mechanism: Shortens T1 and T2 times of neighbouring protons
  • (water)
  • 3) Effects: High signal in T1 and low signal in T2
  • 4) Dosage: For liver 0,1 mmol/Kg or 0,2 ml/Kg, rate of 2-3 ml/s –
  • mainly T1 effects!
  • 5) Clearence: kidneys
  • 6) Toxicity: Nefrotoxic in high dosages
  • 7) Constant effects: High T1 signal for all tissues
  • CONCLUSION: Gd enhancement is studied in T1

Extracellular contrast agents (Gd) #26

  • Equilibrium (interstitial) phase
  • 1) Starts at 90 s from Gd injection (up to 5 min)
  • 2) The liver parenchima loses gradually and homogenously contrast
  • Characteristics:
  • 1. Cysts have no contrast uptake
  • 2. Hemangiomas continue the centripetal contrast filling (high signal)
  • 3. Late central hyposignal in some FNHs (central scar)
  • 4. Peripheral washout in metastasis
  • 5. Washout towards hyposignal small HCCs
  • 6. Late inhomogenous washout or capsular hypersignal in HCCs
  • 7. Hypersignal in peritoneal metastasis
  • 8. Peripheral hypersignal in superficial cholangiocarcinomas
  • ESSENTIAL: Fat signal suppression

NEED FOR A FAST SEQUENCE! #53
